historyTimeline.h2: Range Rover TDV6 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the TDV6 launched in the Range Rover lineup, it introduced a compact, powerful V6 diesel architecture that replaced older inline-six and V8 diesels, offering a refined blend of luxury comfort and serious off-road torque.

milestones.description: 276DT (2.7L, 190hp) introduced in the Range Rover L322 facelift, co-developed with PSA/Ford to improve fuel economy and refinement.
Minor updates to the 276DT architecture to improve reliability, emissions compliance, and turbocharger durability.
306DT (3.0L, 249hp) introduced in the all-new Range Rover L405, featuring twin-turbo technology, a revised block, and significantly improved performance.
Present - Power output of the 306DT increased to 258hp (and up to 275hp in certain later trims), maintaining its status as the core diesel engine for the flagship Range Rover.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Range Rover TDV6 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover TDV6 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 306DT and 276DT engines dominating the Range Rover TDV6 are prized for their torque and refinement, but they are susceptible to specific, well-documented mechanical weaknesses. Rebuilt Range Rover TDV6 engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Crankshaft Bearing & Oil Pump Failure - Why the Range Rover TDV6 Suffers Bottom-End Wear
problems.rootCause: Tin-aluminium coating fatigue on the crankshaft bearings, compounded by oil pump housing weaknesses, can lead to a sudden drop in oil pressure and catastrophic bottom-end failure if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the oil pump and housing, flushing the system, and verifying oil pressure.
repairOptions.longevity: Only suitable if caught early and the crankshaft shows zero signs of scoring or bearing wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt 276DT/306DT with upgraded bottom-end components, revised oil pump, and a 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if crankshaft scoring is present, bearing knock is audible, or the engine has suffered catastrophic failure.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Classic Range Rover L322 TDV6 (2005-2012) values typically range from £4,000 to £12,000, while modern Range Rover L405 TDV6 (2012-present) values range from £14,000 to £55,000+ depending on specification and mileage [THIRD-PARTY]. - Vehicle worth under ~£8,000 (e.g., older L322): repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. Evaluate scrap value first if the vehicle is sub-£6,000. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth £15,000+ (e.g., L405): rebuilt replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value ( Safe).
problems.recommendation: If your Range Rover TDV6 is only showing early signs of oil pressure fluctuation but has strong compression and no metallic knocking, a specialist oil pump replacement and system flush is the most cost-effective route. However, if the engine has suffered severe bearing wear or a spun bearing, a full rebuilt unit with upgraded components is the only reliable long-term solution.

faq.h2: Range Rover TDV6 Engine Replacement - Frequently Asked Questions
faq.intro: Everything Range Rover TDV6 owners usually ask before choosing a rebuilt, reconditioned or used replacement engine.

items.question: How much does a Range Rover TDV6 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned or rebuilt TDV6 engine for the Range Rover typically costs between £5,000 and £11,000 for the supply-only unit in the UK.
keyPoints: Used TDV6 engines start around £2,800 but carry higher risk due to age and mileage.
Rebuilt units with upgraded bottom-end components sit at the £6,500-£11,000 mark.
Supply and fit labour will add £975-£1,300 depending on the specialist.
items.cta: -> Get free quotes for your Range Rover TDV6 engine replacement.

items.question: What are the signs of crankshaft or oil pump failure in a Range Rover TDV6?
items.answer: The TDV6 architecture is prone to bearing wear and oil pump housing weaknesses. Watch for early warning signs before catastrophic failure occurs.
keyPoints: A distinct metallic knocking or rattling noise from the lower engine block, especially on cold starts.
Illuminated oil pressure warning light or fluctuating oil pressure gauge readings.
Sudden loss of power or engine seizing due to oil starvation.
items.cta: -> Compare specialist quotes to fix your Range Rover TDV6 bottom-end issues.

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in a classic Range Rover L322 TDV6?
items.answer: It depends heavily on the vehicle's overall condition and current market value.
keyPoints: Classic L322 TDV6 models typically sell for £4,000 to £12,000.
A £6,500+ rebuilt engine may approach or exceed the value of lower-spec, higher-mileage examples.
For well-preserved examples, a professionally reconditioned engine preserves the vehicle's classic usability and market appeal.
items.cta: -> Check current Range Rover TDV6 replacement costs.

items.question: How long does a Range Rover TDV6 engine replacement take?
items.answer: Because the TDV6 is a densely packed V6 diesel with complex ancillary systems, a specialist workshop requires careful extraction and specific Land Rover diagnostic tools.
keyPoints: Engine removal and refitting usually takes 15 to 20 hours of labour.
Total workshop turnaround is typically 4 to 6 working days, including ECU coding, adaptation, and thorough testing.
items.cta: -> Find a local specialist for your Range Rover TDV6.

items.question: What is the difference between the 2.7 TDV6 and 3.0 TDV6 engines?
items.answer: Both are V6 diesel engines, but the 3.0 TDV6 (306DT) is a significantly revised and more robust evolution of the older 2.7 TDV6 (276DT).
keyPoints: The 3.0L variant features twin-turbo technology, producing 249-275hp compared to the 2.7L's 190hp.
The 306DT block was redesigned to address some of the oil pump and cooling weaknesses of the 276DT, though bearing wear remains a known risk on both if maintenance is neglected.
items.cta: -> Get quotes for the correct engine for your Range Rover TDV6.
